thread:
maria: Heads-up — I kicked off a focused microprobe CI sweep for candidate kernels on ampere and h100. Wanted to surface plan and ask about thresholds for noisy seqlen buckets.

ash: Nice. Which seqlen buckets are you sampling?

maria: 8, 32, 128, 512, and a longtail sample at 2048. Each bucket has 200 iterations. We’re toggling prefill vs no-prefill to watch KV cache behavior.

zach: Can you add a small cohort with KV-hit rate forced low? We saw weird latency tail when KV eviction happens.

maria: Good call. I added a low-kv-hit job (10% hits) and a control (95% hits). Both on ampere/h100.

perf-bot: Perf sweep started: run_id=run-20260307-1, kernels=18, archs=[ampere,h100], seqlen_buckets=[8,32,128,512,2048]. Artifacts at s3://redwood-perf/microprobe/run-20260307-1

karthik: Any gating rules for auto-merge? We should avoid flaky wins.

maria: Proposal: require median latency regression < +5% and p95 < +10% across all arch/seqlen combos, and no single bucket with > +15% p95. Also require no increase in CPU host-side stalls (host_cpu_cycle metric).

ash: Sounds reasonable. Where do we land on throughput vs latency tradeoff? Some kernels speed up longseq at cost of shortseq.

maria: We'll compute normalized cost-per-token (latency * 1/token) and if shortseq regression >5% but longseq improvement >10% and cost drops overall, mark as contingent and send to canary rather than auto-merge.

sophia: Small UX ask — can we add a per-kernel artifact with the microprobe flamegraph + KV ops timeline? Makes triage 10x faster.

maria: Yep planning to upload flamegraphs. Current harness emits: perf.trace, kv_ops.tsv, flame.svg, kernel_config.json. Example config snippet: 

```
{\n  "kernel": "kern_v3_opt",
  "batching": {"max_tokens": 2048, "packet_size": 32},\n  "kv_prefill": true
}
```

zach: CI integration — is ci-bot gating branches if run fails thresholds?

ci-bot: CI check started for PR #4872. Waiting for microprobe sweep run-20260307-1. Thresholds: median<=+5%, p95<=+10%, bucket_p95<=+15%.

perf-bot: Sweep finished. Summary (run-20260307-1): 4 kernels flagged as wins, 2 as possibles, 12 neutral/ambiguous. Notable: kern_v3_opt improved 512/2048 p95 on h100 by -18% but worsened seqlen=8 p95 by +9% on ampere. KV-low cohort showed +22% tail on kern_v3_opt (ampere). Artifacts: s3://redwood-perf/microprobe/run-20260307-1/summary.json

maria: Triage notes — kern_v3_opt has KV-eviction spikes when prefill=true on ampere. Might be memory layout causing worse cache lines. Assigning to @zach and @karthik for probe + repro.

karthik: I'll reproduce locally with the harness (cmd below). If repro, we add a microkernel guard to avoid that code path on ampere prefill.

```
# repro command
./microprobe --kernel kern_v3_opt --arch ampere --seqlen 8 --kv-prefill true --iters 1000 --out /tmp/run
```

zach: Repro in perf-lab confirmed. Flame shows spikes correlated with kv_eviction events. Patch idea: tweak linear_probe stride in KV allocator. Will run candidate patch tomorrow.

maria: Thanks. For CI: marking kern_v3_opt as "hold" for auto-merge and adding a flaky tag. Remaining 3 wins will proceed to canary rollout.

ci-bot: PR #4872 updated: microprobe-check=hold. Please attach repro logs to the PR.

sophia: Quick question — do we want nightly to run the low-kv-hit cohort permanently? That adds cost but catches regressions early.

ash: For now keep it weekend-only. If we see frequent KV regressions, escalate to daily.

maria: Agreed. I'll schedule low-kv cohort on weekends and add a dashboard tile for kv_eviction_rate by kernel.

perf-bot: Dashboard link: https://console.redwood/dashboards/perf/microprobe/run-20260307-1

zach: I'll post a short writeup in eng-runtime with the flame svgs + recommended guard.

maria: Perfect. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

perf-bot: Reaction summary: :thumbsup: x4, :eyes: x2, :warning: x1
